slides.title: VocalEyes: Speaker-Aware Augmented Reality Captioning through In-Conversation Registration
slides.highlight: VocalEyes enables speaker attribution in AR captions via in-conversation registration, supporting HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: VocalEyes is an AR captioning system that identifies speakers via natural self-introductions during conversations.
card.key_idea: It uses a modular pipeline combining audio embeddings for identity, LLM-based semantic parsing for registration, and mouth-aspect-ratio tracking for real-time spatial face marking.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=20) showed 88% speaker-identification accuracy and improved participant tracking accuracy from 47.2% (captions only) to 87.3% (complete interface).
card.limitation: The system does not bind voices to face identities, potentially causing mismatches if different people speak and move.

slides.title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance
slides.tldr: LLM-GUIDED WORLD-STATE MISMATCH DETECTION IN HRI
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to identify world-state mismatches between human assumptions and robot models, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction through proactive failure detection and norm-guided repair.

card.one_liner: A framework for early HRI failure detection by treating breakdowns as world-state mismatches (WSMs).
card.key_idea: Uses LLMs to make implicit human assumptions explicit and verifies them against a robot's multimodal, IoT-augmented world model to detect and repair mismatches proactively.
card.evaluation: Evaluated mismatch identification across ten everyday cases; results showed accurate output and highlighted the importance of grounding representations and verification-oriented refinement.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: A Procedure for Classifying Attachments and Affective Social Bonds in Human-Robot Dyads
slides.highlight: This work proposes a standardized, criterion-based procedure to classify human-robot ties as attachments or affective social bonds, providing a rigorous framework for evaluating human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes a standardized, four-question procedure to rigorously classify human-robot ties as attachments, affective social bonds, or no relationship.
card.key_idea: Grounds HRI relationship classification in developmental and neuroendocrine criteria, requiring behavioral evidence of security functions (for attachment) and partner-specific physiological regulation (for affective social bonds).
card.evaluation: Evaluated by applying the procedure to a representative set of published HRI studies to demonstrate that relational claims often exceed evidence.
card.limitation: Certain physiological regulators, like thermal and cardiac co-regulation, are currently infeasible to operationalize with available robot morphologies.

slides.title: Theory of Scene: Breaking the Symmetry Trap in Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
slides.tldr: REDUCING SYMMETRY TRAPS IN MULTI-AGENT COORDINATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces Theory of Scene (ToS) to resolve coordination failures in homogeneous LLM agents, showing improved performance on Overcooked and other agentic benchmarks. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent and improving human-AI teaming via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: Theory of Scene (ToS) enables homogeneous LLM agents to coordinate without communication by deriving shared divisions of labor.
card.key_idea: A training-free schema using 'role gating' to determine ownership and 'task coupling' to infer whether targets require convergence, divergence, or sequential action.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DivvyBench, GovSim, and Overcooked against six baselines (including ToM); ToS outperformed all baselines across every benchmark metric.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: MultiTalk: Scaling Full-Duplex Speech Models to Long, Multi-Party, Bilingual Conversation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a model and datasets for long-form, multi-party bilingual conversations, focusing on addressee selection and turn-taking. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: MultiTalk scales full-duplex speech models to long, multi-party, bilingual conversations using a new synthetic data engine.
card.key_idea: A two-phase training recipe (bilingual pre-training then multi-party fine-tuning) using a 57.6k-hour synthetic corpus of parallel-stream audio with controllable conversational dynamics and bilingual TTS.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via MultiTalkBench (real human recordings) against baselines like Moshi and Qwen3-Omni; Moshi-MTB significantly outperformed baselines, though remained below human performance.
card.limitation: Model performance remains far below human references, indicating substantial headroom for improvement in long-form multi-party interaction.

slides.title: Evaluating the Impact of Adaptive Extended Reality on Human-Robot Interaction Across the Reality-Virtuality Continuum
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that dynamically adjusting the level of virtuality in XR interfaces improves throughput and reduces workload in human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: Adaptive XR interfaces that allow runtime modality switching improve human-robot interaction performance and reduce user workload.
card.key_idea: A Reality-Virtuality Manager enables operators to dynamically shift between AR, AV, and VR modalities while teleoperating a mobile manipulator via a Meta Quest 3.
card.evaluation: Within-participant pick-and-place experiment using task throughput, NASA-TLX, and SUS; results showed dynamic RVC achieved highest throughput and lowest workload.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Agent-Based Evolutionary Dynamics for Mixed Autonomy Weaving Ramps
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODEL FOR MIXED AUTONOMY TRAFFIC
slides.highlight: This work develops an agent-based model using evolutionary game-theoretic rules to study how decentralized vehicle interactions and heterogeneous preferences affect traffic efficiency. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on meso- and societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: An agent-based model demonstrating how decentralized, altruistic CAVs can reach macroscopic equilibrium at weaving ramps.
card.key_idea: Uses a replicator-based evolutionary game update rule and Social Value Orientation (SVO) to bridge microscopic vehicle interactions with macroscopic Wardrop equilibrium traffic theory.
card.evaluation: Validated via simulations (N=1000 agents) and SUMO; results showed 1-2% agreement with closed-form macroscopic predictions across various penetration rates and demand conditions.
card.limitation: Limited to a single weaving ramp using a calibrated affine-cost model with homogeneous learning rates.

slides.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
slides.tldr: GENERALIZABLE TEST-TIME ADAPTATION VIA HARNESS LEARNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces harness learning to refine an agent's executable program using execution feedback, enabling adaptation at test time without parameter updates. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that adapt at test time beyond in-context learning.

card.one_liner: Harness learning trains a proposer model to adapt an agent's executable harness using test-time feedback.
card.key_idea: Formulates harness revision as meta-learning over executable programs, using reinforcement learning (GRPO) to train a proposer to edit code based on execution reports without updating solver parameters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Reasoning Gym and multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultihopQA). Results show generalization to unseen tasks and improvement over a 35B teacher model.
card.limitation: Training relies on prescribed revision prompts and a fixed solver; the benefits of training on revision sequences are inconsistent across settings.

slides.title: HiThink Turn: An Intent-Aware Turn-Taking Control Module for Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: HiThink Turn introduces an intent-aware streaming predictor that separates response intent from semantic completeness to improve interruption handling. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: HiThink Turn improves full-duplex dialogue by separating response intent from semantic completeness for faster interruptions.
card.key_idea: An intent-aware streaming predictor using minimal intent-sufficient prefix supervision, boundary-aware audio truncation, and system playback state conditioning, implemented by fine-tuning Qwen3-ASR with LoRA.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Easy Turn and Full-Duplex-Bench; outperformed baselines in macro accuracy (up to 99.4%) and average interaction rate (0.933).
card.limitation: Performance trails Gemini Live in identifying system-directed speech during 'Talk-to-Other' scenarios.

slides.title: MAESTRO: a Multimodal Auditory-attention Egocentric Speech-TRacking Open corpus
slides.highlight: The MAESTRO corpus provides simultaneous EEG, eye gaze, pupillometry, egocentric video, and head IMU data, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MAESTRO is a new multimodal corpus for auditory attention decoding featuring EEG, gaze, video, and IMU data.
card.key_idea: A dataset with 16 subjects and 100 trials recording synchronous neural and behavioral signals during a four-speaker cocktail party task with varying SNRs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a four-class classification benchmark using a multi-encoder dilated CNN; results show multimodal fusion significantly outperforms EEG-only decoding.
card.limitation: The baseline model is intended as a lower bound rather than state-of-the-art performance.

slides.authors: K M Naimul Hassan et al.

slides.title: BlenDAgger: Blended Shared Control for Interactive Imitation Learning
slides.tldr: BLENDED SHARED CONTROL FOR IMITATION LEARNING
slides.highlight: BlenDAgger uses shared control to blend human and policy actions during interventions, improving autonomous performance and data collection efficiency. This approach is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation and aligning intent via shared control.

card.one_liner: BlenDAgger improves robot manipulation policies by blending human corrections with policy actions during interactive imitation learning.
card.key_idea: An adaptive arbitration function blends human and robot actions based on cosine similarity, policy uncertainty (via k-NN), and intervention magnitude to ensure smoother, in-distribution corrections.
card.evaluation: Tested on five tasks (2 real-world, 3 simulation) against HG-DAgger; showed 30%+ higher success in real-world tasks and faster data collection (n=14 user study).
card.limitation: Performance gains are limited when training on non-expert data, and arbitration parameters/DoF groupings are currently fixed rather than learned.

slides.title: PUBG Ally: A Conversational Embodied Agent as an AI Teammate
slides.tldr: CONVERSATIONAL EMBODIED AGENT AS AI TEAMMATE
slides.highlight: This work presents an embodied agent that combines real-time game control with natural voice interaction, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PUBG Ally is a voice-enabled AI teammate for PUBG that reasons and acts autonomously alongside players.
card.key_idea: A dual-system architecture combining a language-model agent (System 2) for high-level reasoning/speech via tools and a behavior-tree layer (System 1) for real-time control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via player preferences, surveys across 141 countries, and 39k real-player sessions; positive recommendation responses exceeded negative by 25.1 percentage points.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Guangdong Announces International Humanoid Robot Basketball Tournament
slides.highlight: An international humanoid robot basketball tournament in Guangzhou demonstrates embodied AI capabilities relevant to RwB.

slides.title: mmHRI: Towards Privacy-Preserving Human-Robot Interaction with Millimeter-Wave Radar
slides.highlight: This work introduces mmHRI, a framework using millimeter-wave radar to enable human-robot interaction without RGB cameras, supporting the RwB goal of developing social robots for privacy-critical environments.

card.one_liner: mmHRI enables privacy-preserving robot interaction by using mmWave radar to sense human intent through occlusions.
card.key_idea: A dual-stream architecture fuses raw radar tensors and point clouds, using a memory state-space model (MSSM) to estimate human poses and actions for VLA-based control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a custom radar dataset and real-robot trials; achieved 85.09% action-recognition accuracy under occlusion, outperforming existing radar-based baselines.
card.limitation: Cannot handle multiple subjects, perform radar-only grasping, or physically interact with curtains to open them.

slides.title: MetaCtrl: Your Large Language Models Can Reason Better and More Concisely with a Metacognitive Controller
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE METACOGNITIVE CONTROL FOR LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: MetaCtrl introduces a lightweight controller that adaptively regulates reasoning traces to improve accuracy and reduce redundancy, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: MetaCtrl is a lightweight controller that improves LRM accuracy while significantly reducing reasoning length.
card.key_idea: A learned meta-level controller uses GRPO and a correctness-gated efficiency reward to dynamically apply four interventions (Continue, Fast Think, Skip Think, Stop Think) to a frozen reasoner.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seven math, science, and code benchmarks. Results show accuracy gains (e.g., +4.7 pts on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) and substantial length reduction (53.3%).
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Toborlife AI Launches Full-Body Teleoperation System for Unitree G1 Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: Toborlife AI has introduced a full-body teleoperation system for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, providing insights into human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Positional choice and robust collective behavior in fish schools: biohybrid experiments and modeling
slides.highlight: This research proposes a model for collective behavior that integrates social cohesion with individual exploratory components, relevant to MIMIC's focus on agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A new biohybrid model shows that fish schooling requires both social cohesion and individual exploratory behavior.
card.key_idea: The proposed 'generalized cohesion model' adds an exploratory positional preference term to classical force-based rules, making the model robust to parameter perturbations.
card.evaluation: Compared biohybrid experiments (live fish vs. robotic school) with simulations across $10^5$ parameter combinations using a discrepancy measure $\rho$.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Explore, Execute, Evolve: A Skill Acquisition and Reuse Loop for Embodied Agents
slides.highlight: The RoboSkill framework introduces an Explore, Execute, Evolve loop for skill acquisition and reuse, utilizing tactile feedback and reusable code to improve task success and efficiency. This aligns with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and the use of multi-view feedback to enhance human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: RoboSkill improves robotic task success and efficiency via a loop of skill acquisition, reuse, and evolution.
card.key_idea: A framework using an Explore-Execute-Evolve loop that stores skills as textual guidance and reusable code, complemented by tactile feedback for physical interaction.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO-10 and real robots using four LLM agents; showed 12.5–25.0% higher first-episode success and 7.6–72.4% runtime reduction in simulation.
card.limitation: Skill refinement gains are not always monotonic across successive updates.

slides.title: "Black Mirror?": Public Sensemaking of AI-Powered Lifelogging
slides.highlight: This study examines public discourse on AI-powered lifelogging wearables, providing insights into user concerns regarding privacy, surveillance, and social implications relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception.

card.one_liner: Study of public perceptions of AI-powered lifelogging wearables using social media discourse as an empirical lens.
card.key_idea: Combined topic clustering (BERTopic, LDA) with inductive thematic analysis of 5,053 English and Chinese social media comments regarding the Looki L1 wearable camera.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 2,711 English and 2,342 Chinese comments from TikTok, Instagram, and Xiaohongshu; results identify shared dystopian fears and culturally distinct sociopolitical anxieties.
card.limitation: The study focuses on a single product (Looki L1), so findings may not generalize to other AI-powered lifelogging wearables.

slides.title: Socialality Anchors: Towards Group-bounded Trajectory Prediction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a trajectory prediction framework using interpretable anchors to model agent-specific and context-adaptive grouping, supporting HyECHO's goals in social perception and group state modeling.

card.one_liner: Socialality improves trajectory prediction using context-adaptive, agent-specific grouping rules and interpretable social anchors.
card.key_idea: A duo-scalar-controlled grouping kernel using historical observations and future trajectory previews to learn dynamic, agent-specific grouping rules for in-group and out-of-group interaction modeling.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on standard benchmarks via performance gains, qualitative analyses, and statistical studies of anchor distributions to verify stability and interpretability.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: OTRetarget: Joint Robot and Object Motion Retargeting via Optimal Transport
slides.tldr: JOINT ROBOT-OBJECT MOTION RETARGETING VIA OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
slides.highlight: This work uses entropic optimal transport to jointly retarget robot and object motions from human demonstrations, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: OTRetarget jointly retargets robot and object motions using optimal transport to preserve surface-level interactions.
card.key_idea: Uses entropic optimal transport to map proximity triples (signed distance, witness points, directions) between human and robot geometries, solved via constrained inverse kinematics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AMASS and OMOMO datasets; achieved 87% Jaccard score and 8.7mm depth error, significantly outperforms OmniRetarget in interaction fidelity and runtime.
card.limitation: Self-collision is disabled by default, leading to some self-penetration in locomotion tasks.

slides.title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
slides.tldr: LATENT REASONING FOR EMPATHETIC SPOKEN DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: LoopSLM uses recurrent latent reasoning to bridge the perception-reasoning gap in spoken dialogue, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goals of improving AI teammate adaptation and intent inference via paralinguistic grounding.

card.one_liner: LoopSLM enables high-quality empathetic spoken dialogue by moving paralinguistic reasoning into recurrent decoder depth.
card.key_idea: Combines a looped Transformer for latent reasoning with 'ReCue' for per-pass acoustic grounding, using a two-stage training curriculum to separate reasoning from response generation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on EchoMind, SD-Eval, MMSU, and MMAU-Pro against Qwen2.5-Omni and others; showed superior reasoning accuracy and lower latency than CoT-SFT.
card.limitation: Increasing recurrence depth beyond a certain point (e.g., R=6) can degrade format adherence and reasoning accuracy.
